assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marsupials like kangaroos have a special pouch on their belly where they carry their babies.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a marsupial pouch but does not address reproduction by live birth versus egg-laying, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marsupials like kangaroos have a special pouch on their belly where they carry their babies.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mammal (marsupial) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups; it only gives a single fact about marsupials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marsupials like kangaroos have a special pouch on their belly where they carry their babies.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The pouch is an outer body part, but the competency focuses on parts like head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and food gathering. The pouch's role in carrying young is not the targeted function.

copy.en: Marsupials like kangaroos have a special pouch on their belly where they carry their babies.
copy.tl: Ang mga marsupial gaya ng kangaroo ay may natatanging supot sa tiyan kung saan dinadala nila ang kanilang anak.
copy.bis: Ang mga marsupial sama sa kangguro adunay espesyal nga supot sa tiyan diin ilang gidala ang ilang mga anak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mass measures how much matter is inside an object!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines mass as the amount of matter in an object, but the competency requires describing matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The card does not address the definition of matter or the property of taking up space; it only discusses mass, a related concept.

copy.en:
What is mass?

Mass measures how much matter is inside an object! A large rock has more mass than a small one of the same type, and it never changes no matter where you take it.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mass?

Ang mass ay sumusukat kung gaano karaming matter ang nasa loob ng isang bagay! Ang malaking bato ay may mas maraming mass kaysa maliit na bato, at hindi ito nagbabago kahit saan mo dalhin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mass?

Ang mass nagsukat kung unsa kadaghan ang matter sulod sa usa ka butang! Ang dakong bato adunay mas daghang mass kaysa gamayng bato, ug dili kini magbag-o bisan asa nimo dad-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: weight is the pull of gravity on that matter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines weight as the pull of gravity, which touches on gravity as a force, but it does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or explain how it affects the behaviors of materials/objects in predictable ways. It is a mass-vs-weight distinction, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: Mass is the amount of matter inside you, while weight is the pull of gravity on that matter!
copy.tl: Ang masa ay ang dami ng bagay, pero ang timbang ay ang hila ng grabidad sa bagay na iyon!
copy.bis: Ang masa mao ang gidaghanon sa butang, apan ang gibug-aton mao ang bira sa grabidad niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Place your materials where every group member can safely reach them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a practical tip about arranging materials for group work, but does not describe any of the steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings). It only tangentially relates to the 'materials' aspect of the competency.

copy.en: Place your materials where every group member can safely reach them. This way, your doing steps won't turn into a fight over one spoon!
copy.tl: Ilagay ang materials kung saan maabot ng lahat nang safe. Para hindi mag-away sa isang kutsara habang ginagawa ang steps!
copy.bis: Ibutang ang materials diin maabot sa tanan nga luwas, aron dili mag-away sa usa ka kutsara samtang gibuhat ang steps!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: He predicted that light is an electromagnetic wave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that light is an electromagnetic wave. It does not describe EMR as energy created by vibrations of electrically charged particles or as transverse waves, which are the core elements of G9-F-10. The statement is a related fact but does not directly support the competency's descriptive skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: He predicted that light is an electromagnetic wave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: G9-F-11 requires comparing relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves. The card only identifies light as an electromagnetic wave and provides no comparison of wavelengths or frequencies, nor any mention of other EM wave types. It is only topically related.

copy.en:
What did James Clerk Maxwell predict about light?

He predicted that light is an electromagnetic wave!
copy.tl:
Ano ang hinulaan ni James Clerk Maxwell tungkol sa liwanag?

Hinulaan niya na ang liwanag ay isang electromagnetic wave o alon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gipangtagna ni James Clerk Maxwell bahin sa kahayag?

Giptagna niya nga ang kahayag usa ka electromagnetic wave o balud!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The maya bird helps out in gardens by eating pesky insects — though it does have a habit of pecking at seeds too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the maya eats insects and seeds, which touches on diet, but it does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to do so. It is a single anecdotal fact, not instructional support for the grouping skill.

copy.en: The maya bird helps out in gardens by eating pesky insects — though it does have a habit of pecking at seeds too.
copy.tl: Nakakatulong ang maya sa hardin dahil kumakain ito ng mga insektong peste — kahit mahilig din itong tumuka ng buto.
copy.bis: Ang maya makatabang sa tanaman kay mokaon kini og mga insektong peste — bisan ganahan usab kini motuka og liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The maya is a tiny bird
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the size of a bird. It does not use a table, does not classify living things into the named groups, and provides no characteristics for classification. The mention of 'bird' is merely a shared vocabulary item.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The maya is a tiny bird
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a living thing (a bird) but does not contrast living vs non-living things, nor give examples of each. It provides no instructional support for the competency's skill of observing and describing the difference.

copy.en: The maya is a tiny bird -- about the size of a child's palm!
copy.tl: Ang maya ay napakaliit na ibon -- halos kasinglaki lang ng palad ng isang bata!
copy.bis: Ang maya gamay kaayo nga langgam -- halos sama ra kadako sa palad sa usa ka bata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mayfly can spend up to two years in water as a nymph — but once it becomes an adult, it only lives for minutes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions two life-cycle stages (nymph and adult) of a mayfly, but it does not use a flow chart to compare stages, and it does not compare multiple animal life cycles as required. Format requirement not met.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mayfly can spend up to two years in water as a nymph — but once it becomes an adult, it only lives for minutes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a mayfly's nymph and adult stages, but G5-L-6 specifically requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants. The mayfly is an insect and no comparison of those groups is provided.

copy.en:
How long does a mayfly live underwater?

A mayfly can spend up to two years in water as a nymph — but once it becomes an adult, it only lives for minutes!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal nabubuhay ang mayfly sa tubig?

Maaaring mabuhay ang mayfly sa tubig bilang nymph nang hanggang dalawang taon — pero pagiging adulto, ilang minuto na lang ang buhay nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang mayfly sa tubig?

Makabuhi ang mayfly sa tubig isip nymph hangtod duha ka tuig — apan human mahimong hamtong, pipila lang ka minuto ang iyang kinabuhi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This was the deadliest eruption of Mayon, and it buried the town of Cagsawa.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card only gives a historical fact about Mayon's 1814 eruption and its impact on Cagsawa. It does not help students identify where the nearest active/inactive volcanoes are located or assess eruption risk to a local community, which is the action in G6-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This was the deadliest eruption of Mayon, and it buried the town of Cagsawa.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a volcano and an eruption but does not describe types of volcanoes by activity, eruption type, or location in the crust. It provides no information needed to perform G8-E-3.

copy.en:
When was Mayon's deadliest eruption?

It happened in 1814! This was the deadliest eruption of Mayon, and it buried the town of Cagsawa.
copy.tl:
Kailan ang pinakanakamamatay na pagputok ng Mayon?

Nangyari ito noong 1814! Iyan ang pinakamapanganib na pagputok na bumaon sa bayan ng Cagsawa.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a ang labing makamatay nga pagbuto sa Mayon?

Nahitabo kini niadtong 1814! Kini ang labing makamatay nga pagbuto nga milubong sa lungsod sa Cagsawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rope waves and sound waves are both mechanical!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that rope waves and sound waves are both mechanical and require a medium, but it does not identify them as transverse or longitudinal, nor does it compare their differences and similarities as required by G6-F-7. It only touches on a shared property of these wave types.

copy.en: Rope waves and sound waves are both mechanical! They need a material medium to travel, unlike light which does not need one.
copy.tl: Ang rope waves at sound waves ay parehong mechanical! Kailangan nila ng material medium, hindi tulad ng light na hindi kailangan.
copy.bis: Ang rope waves ug sound waves pareho nga mechanical! Nanginahanglan sila ug material medium, dili sama sa light nga dili kinahanglan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Always check a medicine's expiry date — never take medicine that has passed that date.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about checking medicine expiry dates for personal safety, not about minimizing harmful changes in materials (e.g., burning waste, handling reactive materials). It shares the broad theme of safe handling but does not teach the competency's specific content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Always check a medicine's expiry date — never take medicine that has passed that date.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses avoiding expired medicine, which is a safety practice, but the competency focuses on explaining how changes in materials (e.g., trash disposal, burning household materials) can be harmful to living and non-living things. The card does not explain harmful changes in materials or their environmental impact.

copy.en: Always check a medicine's expiry date — never take medicine that has passed that date.
copy.tl: Laging tingnan ang petsa ng expiry ng gamot — huwag uminom ng gamot na lampas na sa petsang iyon.
copy.bis: Kanunay tan-awa ang petsa sa expiry sa tambal — ayaw pag-inom og tambal nga lapas na nianang petsaha.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strength like '500 mg,'
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions '500 mg' as an example of strength on a paracetamol label, but it does not teach how to identify or appropriately use units such as milligrams in simple science activities. The focus is on reading a medicine label, not on measuring or using units.

copy.en: A paracetamol label shows its name, strength like '500 mg,' and its use — like fever or headache — to help your parents use it right.
copy.tl: Sa label ng paracetamol makikita mo ang pangalan, lakas na tulad ng '500 mg,' at gamit nito — para sa lagnat o sakit ng ulo — para magamit ito ng tama ng magulang mo.
copy.bis: Sa label sa paracetamol makita nimo ang ngalan, kusog sama sa '500 mg,' ug gamit niini — para sa hilanat o sakit sa ulo — aron magamit kini og husto sa imong ginikanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: other meerkats help care for pups that aren't their own while the parents go hunting
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: other meerkats help care for pups that aren't their own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

copy.en: In a meerkat group, other meerkats help care for pups that aren't their own while the parents go hunting.
copy.tl: Sa grupo ng meerkat, tumutulong ang iba sa pag-aalaga ng anak ng kapwa meerkat habang nangangaso ang mga magulang.
copy.bis: Sa grupo sa meerkat, motabang ang uban sa pag-atiman sa mga anak sa uban samtang nangayam ang mga ginikanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: special memory cells remember it, so your defense is much faster if that same germ ever comes back
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not describing how muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: special memory cells remember it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: After your body fights off a germ, special memory cells remember it, so your defense is much faster if that same germ ever comes back.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos labanan ng katawan ang isang germ, may mga memory cell na naaalala ito, kaya mas mabilis ang depensa kapag bumalik ang parehong germ.
copy.bis: Human makig-away ang lawas sa usa ka kagaw, adunay memory cells nga makahinumdom niini, mao nga mas paspas ang depensa kon mobalik ang samang kagaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: He was an Austrian monk and scientist too!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Gregor Mendel as a scientist but does not mention any invention or discovery, which is the core of the competency. It only provides his nationality and occupation, so it does not directly support identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en:
Who was Gregor Mendel?

He was an Austrian monk and scientist too!
copy.tl:
Sino si Gregor Mendel?

Isa siyang Austrian na monghe (monk) at siyentipiko din!
copy.bis:
Kinsa si Gregor Mendel?

Usa siya ka Austrian nga monghe (monk) ug siyentista sab!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The planet Mercury and the metal mercury are totally different!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that Mercury is a planet and distinguishes it from the metal. It does not describe the solar system's structure, Mercury's main features, or its composition, so it does not directly support G5-E-11.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The metal is a liquid used in old thermometers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the metal mercury is a liquid, which touches on one state of matter, but it does not identify the three states (solid, liquid, gas) or teach the concept of states of matter. It is only tangentially related to G5-M-2.

copy.en: The planet Mercury and the metal mercury are totally different! The metal is a liquid used in old thermometers, but they just share the same English name.
copy.tl: Magkaiba ang planetang Mercury at ang metal na mercury! Ang metal ay likidong ginagamit sa lumang termometro, pero pareho lang sila ng pangalan sa Ingles.
copy.bis: Lahi ang planetang Mercury ug ang metal nga mercury! Ang metal likido nga gigamit sa karaang termometro, pero pareho ra sila og ngalan sa Iningles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most meteors, or shooting stars, burn up in the mesosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that meteors burn up in the mesosphere. It does not distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, nor does it describe how they help understand the nature and formation of the Earth and Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most meteors, or shooting stars, burn up in the mesosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about meteors burning in the mesosphere and has no connection to how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere.

copy.en: Most meteors, or shooting stars, burn up in the mesosphere before they can ever reach the ground!
copy.tl: Sa mesosphere nasusunog ang karamihan ng mga meteor o bulalakaw bago pa man umabot sa lupa!
copy.bis: Sa mesosphere masunog ang kadaghanan sa mga meteor o bulalakaw sa dili pa makaabot sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: metal is a good conductor of heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides an example of heat conduction (metal spoon heating up in hot soup) but does not identify it as advantageous or disadvantageous, which is the core action of the competency. It only explains the mechanism, not the benefit or drawback.

copy.en:
Why does the end of a metal spoon get hot when left in hot soup?

It gets hot because metal is a good conductor of heat, letting the heat travel up the spoon!
copy.tl:
Bakit umiinit ang dulo ng metal na kutsara kapag iniwan sa mainit na sabaw?

Umiinit ito dahil konduktor ang metal ng init, kaya nailipat ang init pataas sa kutsara!
copy.bis:
Nganong moinit ang tumoy sa metal nga kutsara kung ibilin sa init nga sabaw?

Moinit kini kay konduktor ang metal sa init, mao nga moagi ang init pataas sa kutsara!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most metals are dense
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a general property of metals (density) but does not identify specific metals used by the local community (iron, gold, silver, copper) or their uses, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most metals are dense
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes one physical property (density) of metals, but the competency asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Density is not among the listed examples and the card does not address the broader set of properties or other solid materials.

copy.en:
Why do most metals feel surprisingly heavy for their size?

Most metals are dense, which makes them feel heavy for their size compared to other materials!
copy.tl:
Bakit karamihan sa metal ay nakakagulat na mabigat para sa laki nito?

Karamihan sa metal ay dense, kaya mabigat sila para sa laki nito kumpara sa ibang materials!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kasagaran sa metal gibug-at kaayo alang sa ilang gidak-on?

Kasagaran sa metal dense, mao nga bug-at sila alang sa ilang gidak-on kumpara sa ubang materials!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost all metals are solid at room temperature! The only exception is mercury, which is a liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions only solid and liquid states, not the three states (solid, liquid, gas) required by the competency. It does not directly teach that matter exists in three states.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost all metals are solid at room temperature! The only exception is mercury, which is a liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives examples of metals as solid and mercury as liquid, but does not identify objects at home or in the classroom as solid, liquid, or gas. It is about a general property of metals, not classifying everyday objects.

copy.en: Almost all metals are solid at room temperature! The only exception is mercury, which is a liquid.
copy.tl: Halos lahat ng metal ay solid sa karaniwang temperatura! Ang tanging pagbubukod ay mercury, na likido.
copy.bis: Halos tanang metal solido sa kasagarang temperatura! Ang gawas lang mao ang mercury, nga likido.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metamorphic rock usually forms deep in the Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about where metamorphic rock forms (deep, hot, high pressure). The competency requires exploring/collecting rocks and describing similarities/differences in features like texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card does not support observation, collection, or feature comparison; it only provides background about rock formation, which is not the skill being taught.

copy.en: Metamorphic rock usually forms deep in the Earth, where it's very hot and heavy rocks above press down hard!
copy.tl: Ang batong metamorphic ay kadalasang nabubuo sa kalaliman ng Lupa, kung saan napakainit at mabigat ang diin ng mga batong nasa itaas!
copy.bis: Ang batong metamorphic kasagaran mahimo sa kahiladman sa Yuta, diin init kaayo ug bug-at ang diin gikan sa mga bato sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many metamorphic rocks have cool visible bands or stripes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feature of metamorphic rocks (bands) and its cause, but does not involve exploring/collecting rocks or comparing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many metamorphic rocks have cool visible bands or stripes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: classify common rocks from provided samples using a simple rock classification system, such as a dichotomous key
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a fact about metamorphic rock appearance but does not support classifying rocks using a simple classification system or dichotomous key.

copy.en: Many metamorphic rocks have cool visible bands or stripes! This happens because strong pressure forces their minerals to line up neatly.
copy.tl: Maraming metamorphic na bato ang may cool na guhit-guhit o banda! Nangyayari ito dahil pinipiga ng matinding presyon ang mga mineral na maghanay.
copy.bis: Daghang metamorphic nga bato ang adunay nindot nga mga banda o guhit! Mahitabo kini tungod kay ang kusog nga presyon nagpahan-ay sa mga mineral.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metamorphic rock is often harder and more compact than the original rock it came from!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about metamorphic rock hardness and compactness. It does not support exploring, collecting, or describing similarities and differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by G5-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metamorphic rock is often harder and more compact than the original rock it came from!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hardness, which is a physical property, but G3-M-5 is about describing physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable in a general materials context. The card gives no instructional support for describing properties of solid materials; it only states a rock-specific fact.

copy.en: Metamorphic rock is often harder and more compact than the original rock it came from!
copy.tl: Kadalasan, mas matigas at mas siksik ang batong metamorphic kaysa sa orihinal na bato na pinagmulan nito!
copy.bis: Kasagaran, mas gahi ug mas siksik ang batong metamorphic kaysa sa orihinal nga bato nga gigikanan niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metamorphosis is controlled by hormones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions metamorphosis, a life-cycle process, but does not use a flow chart or compare stages of any animal life cycle. It only states the hormonal control of metamorphosis, which does not directly support the competency's required activity or content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metamorphosis is controlled by hormones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses metamorphosis, which is a life-cycle change, but does not compare the life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants. It provides no information about birth, egg, seed, or maturation stages, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What controls metamorphosis?

Metamorphosis is controlled by hormones — body chemicals that signal an insect exactly when it's time to change form.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagkontrol sa metamorphosis?

Ang metamorphosis ay kinokontrol ng mga hormone — mga kemikal sa katawan na nagsasabi sa insekto kung kailan na dapat magbago ng anyo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagkontrolar sa metamorphosis?

Ang metamorphosis gikontrolar sa mga hormone — mga kemikal sa lawas nga nagsulti sa insekto kanus-a na oras nga mag-usab og porma.

Many millipedes release a smelly chemical liquid when attacked — enough to drive away animals that want to eat them!
